sample_plan.subpopulation_description: Adults ages 18–39 who prefer researching and arranging travel themselves or keeping a package flexible; includes detailed independent planners and travelers who plan essentials while leaving time open.

travel_planning_style: Wants to plan every detail independently, researching flights, hotels, trains, restaurants, and attractions and using a package only if it saves money or effort.
Enjoys researching extensively and building a detailed itinerary but appreciates expert advice, useful booking tools, and help coordinating complex transfers.
Plans the main flights, lodging, and a few must-see activities independently, leaving meals and much of each day open.
Prefers a flexible package that bundles essential logistics while allowing independent choices, optional excursions, and unstructured time.

sample_plan.subpopulation_description: Adults ages 18–39 who prefer advance structure or help coordinating a Europe package, from a clear prearranged itinerary to substantial delegation with access to the rationale and costs.

travel_planning_style: Likes a clear itinerary with major arrangements handled in advance but wants to decide some daily activities as the trip unfolds.
Prefers a travel advisor or package provider to arrange flights, lodging, transfers, and reservations, while retaining approval over major choices.
Wants nearly all planning delegated to a trusted professional, including itinerary design and problem-solving, because time or confidence is limited.
Has little interest in planning and prefers a guided, all-inclusive or highly organized itinerary with straightforward instructions and few decisions.
Is comfortable delegating logistics but wants access to the itinerary, costs, and decision-making rationale rather than feeling excluded from the process.

U.S.-resident parent or guardian aged 18–49 who enjoys reading books and has a qualifying 4-year-old child (48–59 months); shares books with the child 4–7 days per week, with reading aloud most days or several times each week. Parent enjoyment of books ranges from avid to reading when circumstances permit.

enjoyment_of_reading_books: Enjoys reading very avidly, often choosing books in preference to other leisure activities and regularly seeking out new authors or topics.
Reads for pleasure several times a week and considers books an important source of entertainment, learning, comfort, or reflection.
Enjoys books and reads when time and circumstances permit, though work, caregiving, or other responsibilities make reading irregular.
parent_child_reading_practice: Reads aloud with the child most days, allowing the child to choose books, ask questions, and revisit favorite stories.
Shares books several times each week, often as part of a bedtime, after-school, or weekend routine.

sample_plan.subpopulation_description: U.S.-resident parent or guardian aged 18–49 who enjoys reading books and has a qualifying 5-year-old child (60–71 months); shares books with the child 0–3 days per week, occasionally or while facing barriers to reading together more often. Has a modest but genuine interest in books and reads occasionally, often preferring accessible, short, recommended, or especially engaging titles.
Enjoys books despite substantial barriers such as limited time, fatigue, disability, limited access, or a preference for audio and other accessible formats.
parent_child_reading_practice: Reads with the child occasionally when time and energy allow, without a consistent daily schedule.
Would like to read with the child more often but faces barriers such as work schedules, fatigue, limited access to books, language differences, or competing care needs.

sample_plan.subpopulation_description: U.S. adults ages 18–90 considering or seeking a Europe travel package, in the severe-constraint or tight-budget financial categories, and in a solo, non-partner companion, partner-unavailable, or changing/nonconventional relationship context. Focuses on practical, cost-conscious hotel and package choices. The quantity follows the supplied illustrative financial weights, with an even relationship-context split within this financial tier; it is not an empirical joint estimate.

partner_status: Is single and expects to travel alone, valuing independence while wanting clear information about solo occupancy costs, safety, and opportunities to meet others.
Is single and may travel with a friend, sibling, relative, or organized group rather than a romantic partner.
Has a partner who may not be able or willing to travel, so is considering going alone or with friends and relatives.
Is separated, divorced, widowed, or otherwise not currently partnered and is reassessing what kind of travel feels comfortable and enjoyable.
Has a complicated or changing relationship situation and prefers travel arrangements that do not assume a conventional couple or fixed travel companion.
financial_situation: Faces severe financial constraints, has little discretionary income, and would need a low-cost package, careful saving, or substantial advance planning to make the trip possible.
Has a tight budget and must weigh travel costs against rent, debt payments, family needs, and other essentials; discounts and predictable total pricing matter greatly.
luxury_preferences: Prefers simple, practical travel: a clean and safe place to sleep, reliable transport, and worthwhile experiences matter more than décor, status, or premium service.
Enjoys comfortable basics and small conveniences, such as a private bathroom, good bedding, breakfast, and a helpful front desk, but does not seek extravagance.
Dislikes conspicuous luxury and prefers locally rooted, understated accommodation and experiences even when the budget could support more expensive options.
Avoids costly extras and may feel uncomfortable in highly formal or exclusive settings, preferring welcoming, unpretentious service.
hotel_amenities: Needs only a clean, secure room with a comfortable bed, functioning bathroom, heating or cooling, and a convenient route to transit or main attractions.
Prefers basic amenities such as reliable Wi-Fi, daily housekeeping, luggage storage, and a staffed reception, with no need for extensive facilities.
Would rather stay in a simple, low-cost room and spend the savings on food, museums, events, or excursions.
travel_budget_and_value_orientation: Needs the lowest feasible total cost and compares package prices closely, accepting basic accommodation or inconvenient timing to stay within budget.
Sets a strict spending cap and wants all fees, meals, transfers, and optional activities disclosed in advance to avoid surprises.
Has a fixed budget supplied by an employer, family member, gift, or savings goal and must choose a package that fits that specific limit.
package_inclusions_preference: Wants a basic package covering flights and accommodation, with other choices left open and separately priced.
Wants flights, lodging, and essential transfers bundled to simplify logistics while keeping meals and activities flexible.
Wants the option to remove unwanted inclusions, since paying for activities or services they will not use feels wasteful.

sampled_values.age_group: An older adult aged 65 or above, including active retirees, people continuing to work, and people with a wide range of support and health needs.
technology_and_screen_use: Uses smartphones, computers, streaming, and social media frequently for work, relationships, entertainment, information, and everyday tasks.
Uses social media several times a day to keep up with friends, family, news, or interest communities, while sometimes feeling distracted by it.
Spends extensive time on screens late into the night and finds it difficult to disengage, even when screen use affects sleep or responsibilities.
Plays console, computer, or mobile games regularly, using them for relaxation, competition, storytelling, or social connection.
Is highly skilled with digital tools and adapts quickly to new software, devices, or online services, while remaining alert to privacy and security risks.

sample_plan.subpopulation_description: Older adults aged 65 or above with selective, limited-access, accessibility-focused, avoidant, or minimal technology-use patterns. This is a balanced technology-use coverage contrast, not a prevalence estimate.

sampled_values.age_group: An older adult aged 65 or above, including active retirees, people continuing to work, and people with a wide range of support and health needs.
technology_and_screen_use: Uses technology selectively for practical tasks but prefers face-to-face interaction, printed information, or non-digital leisure when available.
Has limited access to reliable devices, broadband, digital skills, or accessible interfaces, making online services and opportunities harder to use.
Avoids social media and many digital services because of privacy concerns, misinformation, harassment, sensory overload, or personal preference.
Depends on assistive technology, accessibility features, or communication devices to participate in work, education, relationships, or everyday life.
Has minimal technology use, whether through personal choice, age, disability, cost, limited connectivity, or the nature of their work and daily routine.

sample_plan.subpopulation_description: Adults ages 18–39 planning to travel alone, including people who are single, whose partner cannot or will not travel, or whose relationship situation does not imply a companion. A practical, value-conscious package with clear logistics and safety information suits this directive.

partner_status: Is single and expects to travel alone, valuing independence while wanting clear information about solo occupancy costs, safety, and opportunities to meet others.
Has a partner who may not be able or willing to travel, so is considering going alone or with friends and relatives.
Is separated, divorced, widowed, or otherwise not currently partnered and is reassessing what kind of travel feels comfortable and enjoyable.
Has a complicated or changing relationship situation and prefers travel arrangements that do not assume a conventional couple or fixed travel companion.
sampled_values.travel_party_composition: Plans to travel alone and wants a comfortable itinerary with safe transfers, transparent single-room pricing, and optional social activities.
luxury_preferences: Prefers simple, practical travel: a clean and safe place to sleep, reliable transport, and worthwhile experiences matter more than décor, status, or premium service.
Enjoys comfortable basics and small conveniences, such as a private bathroom, good bedding, breakfast, and a helpful front desk, but does not seek extravagance.
Dislikes conspicuous luxury and prefers locally rooted, understated accommodation and experiences even when the budget could support more expensive options.
Avoids costly extras and may feel uncomfortable in highly formal or exclusive settings, preferring welcoming, unpretentious service.
security_concerns_and_adventure_toleranc: Is strongly safety-conscious and researches destinations carefully, favors well-reviewed accommodation, and prefers clear instructions and support contacts.
Takes sensible precautions, buys appropriate insurance, and wants a reliable itinerary while remaining open to ordinary independent exploration.
Feels generally comfortable traveling abroad and balances reasonable safeguards with spontaneous choices and independent time.
Has heightened security concerns due to past experiences, health needs, discrimination concerns, or anxiety, and needs reassurance without being pressured into activities.
hotel_amenities: Needs only a clean, secure room with a comfortable bed, functioning bathroom, heating or cooling, and a convenient route to transit or main attractions.
Prefers basic amenities such as reliable Wi-Fi, daily housekeeping, luggage storage, and a staffed reception, with no need for extensive facilities.
Wants a comfortable hotel with a private bathroom, quality bedding, breakfast options, air conditioning where needed, and helpful local information.
Needs accessibility features such as step-free access, an elevator, roll-in shower or grab bars, clear wayfinding, and staff familiar with accommodation requests.
Prioritizes quiet and rest over facilities, preferring a modest, low-noise property with comfortable bedding and minimal crowds.
Would rather stay in a simple, low-cost room and spend the savings on food, museums, events, or excursions.
travel_planning_style: Wants to plan every detail independently, researching flights, hotels, trains, restaurants, and attractions and using a package only if it saves money or effort.
Enjoys researching extensively and building a detailed itinerary but appreciates expert advice, useful booking tools, and help coordinating complex transfers.
Plans the main flights, lodging, and a few must-see activities independently, leaving meals and much of each day open.
Prefers a flexible package that bundles essential logistics while allowing independent choices, optional excursions, and unstructured time.
Is comfortable delegating logistics but wants access to the itinerary, costs, and decision-making rationale rather than feeling excluded from the process.
social_confirmation: Strongly prefers doing their own thing and chooses destinations and activities based on personal curiosity rather than trends, reviews, or group opinion.
Is independent-minded but checks a few trusted sources for practical reassurance before making a major travel purchase.
Values recommendations from friends and family but makes the final decision according to personal interests and budget.
Relies on reviews, ratings, and travel forums to compare options, while recognizing that other travelers' preferences may differ.
Feels more comfortable choosing a popular, well-reviewed package that many travelers have enjoyed, especially when visiting Europe for the first time.
itinerary_pace: Prefers a very relaxed pace with late starts, ample breaks, limited hotel changes, and no more than one major activity on most days.
Prefers a gentle but purposeful schedule, with a main activity each day and enough free time for meals, rest, and spontaneous discoveries.
Likes a balanced itinerary that includes several highlights but leaves some afternoons or evenings open.
Needs a flexible pace that can change day by day because of health, energy, weather, companions, or uncertain work and family commitments.
travel_budget_and_value_orientation: Needs the lowest feasible total cost and compares package prices closely, accepting basic accommodation or inconvenient timing to stay within budget.
Sets a strict spending cap and wants all fees, meals, transfers, and optional activities disclosed in advance to avoid surprises.
Seeks good value and will pay more for meaningful improvements in location, reliability, comfort, or included experiences.
Balances cost and comfort, choosing a dependable mid-range package with a few optional upgrades rather than the cheapest or most expensive offer.
package_inclusions_preference: Wants a basic package covering flights and accommodation, with other choices left open and separately priced.
Wants flights, lodging, and essential transfers bundled to simplify logistics while keeping meals and activities flexible.
Wants the option to remove unwanted inclusions, since paying for activities or services they will not use feels wasteful.

sample_plan.subpopulation_description: Adults ages 18–39 traveling as a couple, including people dating and considering a first trip together and those in committed or long-term partnerships. This directive focuses on comfortable lodging and a coordinated but flexible package, without assuming the trip is a romantic celebration.

partner_status: Is dating someone and is considering a first or relatively new trip together, with interest in balancing shared activities and personal preferences.
Has a committed partner and expects to travel as a couple, preferring a package that makes it easy to coordinate lodging, meals, and activities.
Is married or in a long-term partnership and treats travel as shared time, while still wanting room for different interests or occasional independent activities.
sampled_values.travel_party_composition: Plans to travel as a couple and prioritizes shared experiences, convenient accommodation, and a manageable balance of sightseeing and downtime.
luxury_preferences: Appreciates sophisticated design, thoughtful details, excellent food, attentive staff, and a sense that the trip has been specially curated.
Actively seeks luxury, including high-end hotels, premium transport, spacious rooms, concierge support, and distinctive experiences with exceptional service.

Actively seeks luxury, including high-end hotels, premium transport, spacious rooms, concierge support, and distinctive experiences with exceptional service.
Is interested in occasional luxury but prefers to spend selectively, choosing one memorable splurge while keeping other parts of the trip practical.
security_concerns_and_adventure_toleranc: Is strongly safety-conscious and researches destinations carefully, favors well-reviewed accommodation, and prefers clear instructions and support contacts.
Takes sensible precautions, buys appropriate insurance, and wants a reliable itinerary while remaining open to ordinary independent exploration.
Feels generally comfortable traveling abroad and balances reasonable safeguards with spontaneous choices and independent time.
Is confident in unfamiliar places, willing to navigate public transportation and try less familiar activities, while maintaining basic safety precautions.
hotel_amenities: Wants a comfortable hotel with a private bathroom, quality bedding, breakfast options, air conditioning where needed, and helpful local information.
Values a central or well-connected location, soundproofing, dependable Wi-Fi, an elevator, good breakfast, and a lounge or other pleasant shared space.
Prefers a full-service hotel with a restaurant, room service, fitness facilities, laundry, concierge help, and flexible check-in or luggage arrangements.
Seeks upscale amenities such as a spa, pool, fine dining, premium toiletries, generous room space, high-touch service, and distinctive design.
Needs accessibility features such as step-free access, an elevator, roll-in shower or grab bars, clear wayfinding, and staff familiar with accommodation requests.
travel_planning_style: Plans the main flights, lodging, and a few must-see activities independently, leaving meals and much of each day open.
Prefers a flexible package that bundles essential logistics while allowing independent choices, optional excursions, and unstructured time.
Likes a clear itinerary with major arrangements handled in advance but wants to decide some daily activities as the trip unfolds.
Prefers a travel advisor or package provider to arrange flights, lodging, transfers, and reservations, while retaining approval over major choices.
Is comfortable delegating logistics but wants access to the itinerary, costs, and decision-making rationale rather than feeling excluded from the process.
social_confirmation: Is independent-minded but checks a few trusted sources for practical reassurance before making a major travel purchase.
Values recommendations from friends and family but makes the final decision according to personal interests and budget.
Relies on reviews, ratings, and travel forums to compare options, while recognizing that other travelers' preferences may differ.
Feels more comfortable choosing a popular, well-reviewed package that many travelers have enjoyed, especially when visiting Europe for the first time.
Likes traveling with a group and sharing experiences, and is influenced by whether friends, relatives, or peers are enthusiastic about the itinerary.
itinerary_pace: Prefers a very relaxed pace with late starts, ample breaks, limited hotel changes, and no more than one major activity on most days.
Prefers a gentle but purposeful schedule, with a main activity each day and enough free time for meals, rest, and spontaneous discoveries.
Likes a balanced itinerary that includes several highlights but leaves some afternoons or evenings open.
Needs a flexible pace that can change day by day because of health, energy, weather, companions, or uncertain work and family commitments.
travel_budget_and_value_orientation: Seeks good value and will pay more for meaningful improvements in location, reliability, comfort, or included experiences.
Balances cost and comfort, choosing a dependable mid-range package with a few optional upgrades rather than the cheapest or most expensive offer.
Will pay a premium for convenience, reduced planning effort, favorable flight times, and high-quality accommodation.
Is willing to spend generously on a distinctive, memorable trip, but expects exceptional service and careful personalization in return.
package_inclusions_preference: Wants flights, lodging, and essential transfers bundled to simplify logistics while keeping meals and activities flexible.
Prefers breakfast and several key excursions included, with free time for independent exploration and dining.
Wants a package with expert-guided tours, museum access, and reservations included, but does not need every meal or hour planned.
Prefers a highly customized package whose inclusions can be adjusted to personal interests, accessibility needs, and budget.
